articles.title: BJP Stages Nationwide Protest Against Kharge's Remarks
articles.description: Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge has sparked a political controversy with remarks made during a speech in Patna, leading to nationwide protests by the BJP. The comments, perceived as targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his late father, have drawn sharp criticism from BJP leaders, who have labeled them as disrespectful and unparliamentary. BJP's Nationwide Protest The controversy began when Kharge responded to an audience member during his speech marking the birth anniversary of Bihar's first Chief Minister, Shri Krishna Singh. The audience member reportedly shouted "Modi Nahi Jayega," prompting Kharge to retort with "Modi ka baap bhi jayega." The BJP has condemned the remarks, calling them an insult to the Prime Minister's family and demanding an apology from the Congress President. In response, BJP workers have staged protests across the country, including in Jammu, Karnataka, and Delhi. Demonstrators have burned effigies of Kharge and marched to Congress offices, accusing the party of engaging in "Gali politics." Meanwhile, Congress leaders have defended Kharge, claiming the remarks were directed at the RSS, the ideological parent of the BJP, rather than Modi's biological father. Political and Legal Fallout The incident has also taken a legal turn, with a BJP worker filing a complaint against Kharge at Patna's Kotwali police station. Congress leaders, including Dhanush Ali, have doubled down on their rhetoric, further escalating tensions. Ali reiterated Kharge's remarks and added that "illegitimate children" involved in alleged electoral fraud would also face consequences. While the BJP has accused Congress of lowering the political discourse, Congress leaders have countered by highlighting past instances of alleged verbal attacks by BJP members. The controversy underscores the growing polarization in Indian politics, with both parties refusing to back down from their respective positions.

articles.title: Europe Looks Beyond America's Nuclear Shield As Macron Offers 10 Countries An Alternative | Report
articles.description: Ten European countries are reportedly discussing a French-led nuclear deterrence initiative as questions grow over whether Europe can continue relying almost entirely on America’s nuclear umbrella. At the centre of the proposal is France’s concept of “forward deterrence,” which could eventually involve French nuclear-capable Rafale fighters operating farther across Europe. Britain, Germany, Poland, Greece and Nordic countries are among those reportedly involved in discussions. France maintains an independent nuclear arsenal, publicly estimated at roughly 290 warheads, giving Emmanuel Macron something most European governments do not possess: a deterrent that does not ultimately depend on a US president authorising nuclear escalation. But control would remain firmly in Paris. Participating countries could potentially host or support the posture, while the French president would retain the final decision over nuclear use. For Washington, the political implication is significant: European interest in a French alternative reflects growing debate over whether America’s security guarantee alone remains sufficient.
